title: transcript.v1
description: The transcript contract: speaker-attributed segments + the session envelopes carried over the bus (bot[TS] → collector[Py]) and the live mutable bundle (gateway → dashboard).

Source.description: How the speaker was attributed. chat = an in-meeting chat message captured into the transcript (speaker = the chat sender; text = the message).

TranscriptSegment.description: One speaker-attributed utterance. Times are seconds relative to session start.

speaker.description: display name (glow-bound or a provisional label)

SessionStart.description: Opens a transcript session on the bus. Auth is transport-layer (not a field here); tenant/owner/visibility are deferred — added additively to this object when sharing lands (ADR-0003).

Transcription.description: A batch of persisted (confirmed) segments → the collector stream.

MutableBundle.description: The live confirmed+pending bundle the gateway forwards verbatim to the dashboard.

StreamEntry.description: One entry of the transcription_segments Redis stream (bot -> collector): the fields an XADD carries. `payload` is the JSON of one bus message (session_start, transcription, transcript_retract, session_end). `auth` and `sig` prove the session may speak for the meeting the payload names: `auth` is the header.payload of the session's MeetingToken (invocation.v1 `token`, whose claims name the meeting) and `sig` is HMAC-SHA256(key = the whole token, message = the `payload` string) as 64 lowercase hex digits. The collector rebuilds the token from `auth` with the secret that minted it, so the bearer never enters Redis, and acknowledges and drops any entry whose token or signature fails or whose payload `meeting_id` is not the token's. A bot older than v0.13.2 writes no `auth`/`sig`, and its entries are dropped. The signer is segment_entry.py in this folder.

SignedEntryVector.description: A signing vector: signing `payload` with `token` must give exactly `auth` and `sig`. The token is a fixture, not a minted MeetingToken.

FeedEntry.description: One entry of the per-meeting feed `tc:meeting:{meeting_id}`, keyed by the meetings-domain numeric row id (never the native id, which collides across users and rows). meeting-api is its only writer: the collector writes a segment, a retraction or a bot's own end marker only for bus entries it admitted (StreamEntry), the lifecycle writes the start and end markers on the meeting's own state changes, and the transcript import writes the end marker of a transcript it stored. So a reader may act on it: agent-api's transcription watcher registers and ends meetings from it, and the terminal's live view reads it through agent-api. The entry's one field, `payload`, is the JSON of a FeedTranscription, a FeedRetract, a FeedSessionStart or a SessionEnd.

FeedSegment.description: One persisted segment as the feed carries it.

FeedTranscription.description: A feed entry carrying one persisted, non-empty segment. `session_uid` and `meeting_id` both hold the meeting's native id for display (the row id when no native id resolves); the key the entry sits under is the row id.

FeedRetract.description: A feed entry withdrawing segments the bot superseded; readers drop them.

FeedSessionStart.description: A feed entry marking the meeting live again on this row: meeting-api writes it when the meeting's lifecycle reaches `active`, so a reader that saw an earlier SessionEnd on a reused row stops treating the row as ended. `session_uid` carries the native id for display (the row id when no native id resolves), as on every other feed entry. Unlike the bus-level SessionStart it carries nothing else.
